$comment: Apollo surface panoramas verified by the DSH agent on 2026-02-13 from the NASA Image and Video Library. Download URLs are written with the http scheme because that is what was measured; https://images-assets.nasa.gov serves the identical file when the proxy is actually in use (NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1). See .agents/research/apollo-surface-panoramas.md for the evidence.
proxyNote: Node 24 ignores HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY unless NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 is also set. Without it requests go direct and the direct route returns 403 for https://images-assets.nasa.gov, which is what produced an earlier, wrong '403' finding.

panoramas.title: Panoramas of Apollo sites — Tranquility Base, looking southwest
panoramas.description: First of a multi-framed panorama photographed from a point some 30 or 40 feet west of the plus-Z (west) footpad of the Lunar Module "Eagle." The view is looking toward the southwest showing part of the horizon crater rim that was pointed out as being visible from the Eagle's window. Created from Apollo 11 magazine 40 frames 5881 through 5891.
panoramas.coverage: partial azimuth; not a full 360° (edge-wrap test negative)
panoramas.notes: Widest Apollo 11 surface panorama in the archive at 30000 px. Sky is blacked to the horizon by NASA retouching, which makes keying it to transparency straightforward. Best single candidate for an Apollo 11 browsable view.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 11 lunar surface photos at Tranquility Base, of a crater Armstrong noted during the Lunar Module descent
panoramas.description: The panoramas were built by combining Apollo 11 images starting with frame AS11-40-5954 through end frame AS11-40-5961. Minimal retouching, including removal of lens flares and blacking out the sky to the lunar horizon.
panoramas.coverage: partial azimuth, roughly 180-200° of the horizon
panoramas.notes: Downloaded and inspected visually: a single continuous stitch, no mosaic seams, Hasselblad reseau crosses present, the Lunar Module with the US flag at the left, a small crater centre, a boulder and the photographer's shadow at the right. 3.5:1 aspect — wider than a 2:1 equirectangular, consistent with a cylindrical sweep under 360°.

panoramas.title: Panoramas of Apollo sites — Apollo 12, northeast of the Lunar Module looking west then counterclockwise into Surveyor Crater
panoramas.description: Image is a view taken from northeast of the Lunar module (LM) looking west at panel and Flag, then to southwest at LM and counterclockwise to south and west looking into Surveyor Crater. Created using Apollo 12 images — mag 47 frames 6982 thru 7006.
panoramas.coverage: partial azimuth; 25 frames suggests a wide sweep
panoramas.notes: Includes Surveyor 3 in frame, which is the interesting content at Apollo 12. Dimensions from NASA metadata, not yet downloaded.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 12 lunar surface photos with lunar module pilot Alan L. Bean and the TV, taken from just inside the rim of Surveyor Crater
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 12 images starting with frame AS12-46-6777 thru end frame AS12-46-6780.
panoramas.notes: The NASA title reads "Apollo 15 lunar panorama" but the description and frame numbers are Apollo 12 magazine 46 — the title is wrong in the archive. Trust the description.

panoramas.title: Panoramas of Apollo sites — Apollo 14, view of the lunar surface towards the western horizon
panoramas.description: View of the Lunar Surface towards the western Horizon. Image was created using Apollo 14 images — mag 66 frames 9271 thru 9293.
panoramas.coverage: partial azimuth; 23 frames suggests a wide sweep
panoramas.notes: The only Apollo 14 surface panorama found in the archive; 30000 px wide makes it the joint-largest with the Apollo 11 and Apollo 16 entries.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 15 lunar surface photos south of Station 2, Astronaut David R. Scott at the Lunar Roving Vehicle on the edge of Hadley Rille
panoramas.description: Taken by lunar module pilot James B. Irwin. Built by combining Apollo 15 images starting with frame AS15-85-11448 thru end frame AS15-85-11453.
panoramas.notes: Contains the LRV and Hadley Rille — visually the strongest Apollo 15 candidate.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Station 8 and Mons Hadley taken during the third moonwalk of the Apollo 15 mission
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 15 images starting with frame AS15-82-11054 thru end frame AS15-82-11058.
panoramas.notes: The only Apollo 15 view that includes Mons Hadley itself.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 15 lunar module pilot James B. Irwin using a scoop in making a trench in the lunar soil during the second moonwalk
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 15 images starting with frame AS15-92-12420 thru end frame AS15-92-12438.
panoramas.notes: Only 1030 px tall — a shallow strip. Low value for a sphere-mapped viewer; keep as a secondary item.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 16 lunar surface photos, Charles M. Duke Jr. collecting lunar samples at Station 1 during the first moonwalk at the Descartes landing site
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 16 images starting with frame AS16-114-18416 thru end frame AS16-114-18431. With significant overlap and time delay between frames, it is possible to create two different versions.
panoramas.coverage: partial azimuth; one of two stitched versions of the same sweep
panoramas.notes: Paired with jsc2012e052599, the alternate stitch of the same frames. Pick one, not both.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 16 lunar surface photos, Charles M. Duke Jr. collecting lunar samples at Station 1 (alternate stitch)
panoramas.description: Same frames as jsc2012e052598; the archive notes two different versions are possible from the overlap.
panoramas.notes: Alternate stitch of the previous entry.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 16 lunar surface photos of Station 10 and Sample 381 Rock, second moonwalk
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 16 images starting with frame AS16-114-18450 thru end frame AS16-114-18467.
panoramas.notes: Only 956 px tall — a shallow strip.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 16 commander John W. Young working at the Lunar Roving Vehicle prior to ALSEP deployment, first moonwalk
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 16 images starting with frame AS16-116-18573 thru end frame AS16-116-18581.
panoramas.notes: Good height-to-width balance; the better Apollo 16 candidate alongside the 30000 px Station 1 pair.

panoramas.title: Panorama view from the Apollo 16 Lunar Module window taken on-orbit during Revolution 16
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 16 images starting with frame AS16-113-18297 thru end frame AS16-113-18307.
panoramas.coverage: orbital view through the LM window; partial azimuth
panoramas.notes: NOT a surface panorama — it is a view from orbit through the LM window, so it does not belong under a landing-site entry. Listed here so nobody mistakes the 18326x8537 size for a surface view.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 17 lunar surface photos — Station 2, EVA 2
panoramas.description: Photo numbers used for this panoramic include: Apollo 17 start frame AS17-138-21053 thru end frame AS17-138-21073. View is of Station 2, taken during the second Extravehicular Activity (EVA) 2.
panoramas.coverage: partial azimuth; edge-wrap test negative, so under 360°
panoramas.notes: Downloaded and inspected. Four 7000 px panels were rendered: the four quadrants show clearly different terrain (a ridge at the left, the parked LRV with astronaut shadows at the right), and a dedicated left-edge/right-edge seam test shows the two ends do NOT join — so this is a partial-azimuth cylindrical panorama, not a 360° wrap. Hasselblad reseau crosses throughout; no visible stitch seams. 9.4:1 aspect.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 17 lunar surface photos — ALSEP Station, EVA 1
panoramas.description: Photo numbers used for this panoramic include: Apollo 17 start frame AS17-147-22572 thru end frame AS17-147-22600. View is of the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiment Package (ALSEP) Station taken during Extravehicular Activity (EVA) 1.
panoramas.coverage: partial azimuth; the most frames of any Apollo panorama here
panoramas.notes: 29 frames is the largest sweep here; worth a wrap test of your own before calling it 360°.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 17 lunar surface photos — Station 1, EVA 1
panoramas.description: Photo numbers: Apollo 17 start frame AS17-136-20745 thru end frame AS17-136-20759. View is of Station 1, taken during EVA 1.
panoramas.notes: Tallest of the wide Apollo 17 entries at 3575 px, which makes it the best Apollo 17 candidate for a sphere-mapped viewer.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 17 lunar surface photos — Station 5, Taurus-Littrow, EVA 2
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 17 images starting with frame AS17-145-22159 through end frame AS17-145-22181.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 17 lunar surface photos — Station 6, EVA 3
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 17 images starting with frame AS17-141-21575 through end frame AS17-141-21603.
panoramas.notes: Downloaded: 9495x1200 (7.9:1), only 1200 px tall. Station 6 is the site of the huge split boulder, so it is the most geologically interesting Apollo 17 station, but the resolution limits how far a viewer can pan up.

panoramas.title: Panorama view of Apollo 17 lunar surface photos — Station 7, EVA 3
panoramas.description: Built by combining Apollo 17 images starting with frame AS17-146-22339 thru end frame AS17-146-22363.
panoramas.notes: 5001 px tall is the tallest surface panorama in the whole set — the best vertical coverage for a browsable view, at 5.4:1.

notYetDownloaded: Dimensions marked dimensionSource=nasa-metadata come from NASA's own metadata.json, which is authoritative but was not re-verified by downloading the file. Fetch and re-measure with `node .agents/img-info.mjs <url>` before committing any asset.
